headline: GOLD SLIDES TO $4,508 — SECOND STRAIGHT WEEKLY LOSS AS IRAN DEAL COLLAPSES AND FED HIKE BETS MOUNT
snippet: Gold fell toward $4,500/oz on Friday, heading for its second consecutive weekly decline as US CPI printed at 3.8% (above forecast), oil prices stayed elevated, and reports that Iran's Supreme Leader would not yield on uranium enrichment rights killed peace-deal hopes. Markets now price roughly 55% odds of a Fed rate hike by October, reducing gold's appeal as a non-yielding asset.

headline: FREEGOLD DRILLS 347 g/t BONANZA AND 115 g/t OVER 3M AT ALASKA'S 17-MILLION-OUNCE GOLDEN SUMMIT
snippet: Freegold Ventures (TSXV: FVL) returned bonanza-grade intercepts at Golden Summit in Alaska including 347.9 g/t Au over 1.4m, 115.85 g/t over 3.1m, and 33.71 g/t over 19.5m in the latest infill holes. The 17.2Moz indicated resource is in the middle of a 50,000m 2026 drill program targeting high-grade corridor definition ahead of a pre-feasibility study.

headline: 82 DEAD: CHINA'S WORST COAL MINE EXPLOSION IN OVER A DECADE ROCKS SHANXI PROVINCE
snippet: A gas explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Changzhi, Shanxi killed at least 82 workers on May 22 after underground carbon monoxide sensors triggered a breach alarm. The mine had been flagged as high-risk for gas content by China's National Mine Safety Administration in 2024. President Xi Jinping ordered a full investigation and demanded accountability under law.

headline: SILVER NEAR $78 — DOWN 37% FROM JANUARY'S ALL-TIME HIGH OF $121.64 AS INFLATION FEARS RETURN
snippet: Silver is trading in the $76–80/oz range as of May 22, having corrected sharply from its January 29 record high of $121.64/oz, dragged by fading ETF inflows and hotter-than-expected US inflation. Despite the pullback, the Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive structural supply deficit for 2026, with industrial demand from solar, EVs, and 5G infrastructure remaining firm.

headline: COPPER RETREATS TO $6.35/LB FROM MAY 13 ALL-TIME HIGH OF $6.65 AS IRAN UNCERTAINTY WEIGHS
snippet: Copper has pulled back to around $6.35/lb from the record close of $6.65 reached on May 13, as skepticism over a US-Iran peace deal kept energy prices and inflation expectations elevated, squeezing manufacturing demand. The metal is still up 31% year-over-year, supported by AI data-center electrification and the global energy transition. Chile's state copper commission Cochilco recently raised its 2026 price forecast to $5.55/lb.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS AT $84/LB AS NEXGEN'S $2.2B ROOK I MINE IN SASKATCHEWAN PREPARES TO BREAK GROUND THIS SUMMER
snippet: Uranium spot traded flat at $84.70/lb on May 22, up 18% year-over-year but off recent highs as utilities remain cautious amid geopolitical uncertainty. NexGen Energy's (TSX: NXE) Rook I project in northern Saskatchewan — Canada's largest development-stage uranium deposit at ~30Mlb/year capacity — received its final federal construction licence in March and is set to break ground this summer in a $2.2B build that would be the first new major Canadian uranium mine in over two decades.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE FALLS 2.2% TO 178,000 CNY/T AS HIGHER PRICES TRIGGER MINE RESTARTS IN CHINA
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate fell to 178,000 CNY/t on May 22, down 2.2% on the day, as a spike to 200,500 CNY/t on May 13 prompted producers to restart idled operations — including Mineral Resources' Bald Hill mine — capping the rally. China's NEV output rose 5.5% year-over-year to 1.32 million units in the latest data, keeping the demand backdrop constructive even as near-term supply is recovering.

headline: GDX AND GDXJ DOWN 25% FROM JANUARY HIGHS — ANALYSTS SPLIT ON WHETHER THE CORRECTION IS OVER
snippet: Gold mining indices GDX and GDXJ have fallen approximately 25% since gold peaked near $5,600/oz in late January 2026, underperforming even gold's own 20% pullback to ~$4,500. Some analysts see deep discounts to NAV in junior miners as a re-entry window; others warn that 55% market odds of a Fed rate hike by October could extend pressure on gold equities through summer. Goldman Sachs maintains a $5,400/oz target for December 2026.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS MAPS HIGH-GRADE GOLD SHOOT IN SURINAME: 30M AT 4.64 g/t AND 12M AT 10.57 g/t
snippet: Founders Metals (TSXV: FDR) confirmed a coherent, plunging high-grade gold shoot at the Maria Geralda target within Suriname's Antino Gold Project, with best intercepts of 30m at 4.64 g/t Au and 12m at 10.57 g/t Au from a 37-hole deep auger program released May 20. The highest-grade gold plunges at 56–60° toward untested bedrock; diamond drilling for bedrock follow-up is planned for Q4 2026.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD & SILVER TERMINATES SPROTT SILVER STREAM IN ~8-MILLION-SHARE SWAP AT GALENA MINE
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA) agreed to terminate its remaining silver delivery obligations to Sprott Mining in exchange for approximately 8 million new shares, eliminating a production-linked cash flow liability tied to its Galena silver-copper mine in Idaho. The deal removes a long-running balance sheet overhang and is expected to improve free cash flow visibility.

headline: GOLDMAN HOLDS $5,400/OZ GOLD TARGET FOR YEAR-END — INSTITUTIONS UNMOVED BY CORRECTION
snippet: Despite gold's retreat from $5,600/oz in January to the current ~$4,500 range, Goldman Sachs is maintaining a $5,400/oz target for December 2026, and several firms model $6,000+ if the US-Iran conflict escalates. GoldSilver.com's analysis points to intact structural drivers — central bank accumulation, de-dollarization, and above-target inflation — and frames the current dip as consolidation rather than trend reversal.

headline: NDPR OXIDE UP 88% YEAR-TO-DATE AT $99/KG — US PROJECT VAULT STOCKPILE ADDS POLICY TAILWIND FOR RARE EARTH STOCKS
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide is trading near $99/kg in May 2026, up 88% from January's ~$53/kg open, as Chinese export controls and accelerating EV magnet demand drove a sharp re-rating. China's official rare earth price index stands at 269.6 while terbium oxide has reached $892/kg. The Trump administration's $12B Project Vault — a critical mineral reserve targeting 60 inputs including rare earths — is providing an additional demand floor for Western producers.
